results.summary: This project implements a 4x4 systolic array matrix multiply-accumulate accelerator in SystemVerilog. It computes C = A x B for two 4x4 matrices of unsigned 8-bit integers, producing 16 results with 20-bit accumulator precision. A control FSM sequences loading matrices over an SPI slave interface and transmitting the truncated 16-bit results back over SPI MISO. The design spans a 2x2 tile area and requires an external SPI master to communicate with the chip.

results.summary: This project is an 8-bit CPU implemented in SystemVerilog with an integrated bootloader and IO. Its ISA supports add, add 1, and, not, jmp, store, load, and nop instructions operating on two registers and a data memory. Programming and communication use a UART interface on the uart_rx and uart_tx pins, matching the UART over demo board USB pinout. An external USB-to-UART converter is required to program the CPU.

results.summary: This design combines an SPI memory controller and a VGA timing core in Verilog. The SPI controller reads bytes from an external SPI RAM using command 0x03 with a 16-bit address, exposing busy and valid status. The VGA core generates 640x480 at 60 Hz timing with hsync, vsync, and 2-bit RGB output. A mode pin selects between raw SPI byte output and VGA timing output, and a cocotb test exercises the SPI path in simulation.

It is designed to be integrated into any SPI or I²C memory controller, with all operations pipelined for efficiency. The design is intended for machine learning inference tasks and is notable for its compact implementation. It is not a general-purpose processor but a dedicated accelerator.
results.summary: This project implements a calculator for a 4x4 matrix keypad in System Verilog. The keypad scanner drives the column lines and reads the row lines to detect key presses, buffering digits and storing operators. An ALU computes addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division, and the 8-bit result is presented on the dedicated output pins. An external 4x4 matrix keypad is required.

results.summary: This project is a simple UART transmitter module written in Verilog. It transmits 8-bit parallel data presented on ui[7:0] at 115200 baud when the tx_send pin is asserted. The TX output pin carries the serial data, and tx_busy indicates transmission activity. No external hardware beyond a UART receiver is required.
